key_insight: The paper turns hyperelastic continuum mechanics into an edge-strain interaction-potential formulation that supports both passive and active tissue dynamics without relying on a full finite-element global nonlinear solve.
engineering_relevance: This provides a faster, discrete solver framework for simulating biologically realistic active soft tissues such as the myocardium while retaining continuum-level energetic consistency.
method: Recast hyperelastic constitutive laws using tetrahedral edge strain rather than independent mass-spring links.
Embed active contraction via active-strain multiplicative decomposition expressed as a time-dependent activated reference configuration.
Add an incompressibility treatment designed to avoid volumetric locking while preserving the energy balance.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical tests across multiple hyperelastic laws and a realistic ventricle case, showing correct energy balance and physiologically consistent longitudinal shortening and wall thickening.
watch_item: Performance and accuracy still depend on how well the edge-based discretization and incompressibility strategy generalize across mesh quality, material law choice, and highly nonlinear loading.
paper_title: An interaction potential method for passive and active dynamics of hyperelastic materials
